newsitem.title: USA: NYS Judge rules NYC must raise workfare pay - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS Judge rules NYC must raise workfare pay - paper.

text.p: A New York State judge has ruled that New York City's workfare system unfairly calculates the number of hours that welfare recipients must work to get benefits, the New York Times said on Tuesday.

The city now bases those hours roughly on the $4.75-an-hour federal minimum wage. For many workers, in exchange for about $100 in welafare benefits each week, they work about 20 hours in jobs like cleaning parks, sweeping sidewalks or doing clerical work.

But Justice Jane Solomon of the New York State Supreme Court, in a decision on Monday, found that the city must base the pay for approximately 35,000 welfare recipients in workfare on what it paid regular city workers for similar tasks, about $8 to $10 an hour in most cases, the paper said.
City officials told the New York Times the judge's decision would be appealed.

Welfare advocates said that if the ruling were upheld, the city would probably cut the number of hours the welfare recipients work, instead of paying them bigger benefits to reflect the prevailing wages.
